# DSPlugins: Scope Planner for Jira Cloud

> DSPlugins makes Scope Planner, a Jira Cloud app built on Atlassian Forge. It puts every issue of a sprint, a backlog or any JQL in one editable table for story points and time estimates, keeps the numbers in a private or team draft, shows exactly what will change, and publishes them to Jira in one pass.

## Facts

- Platform: Jira Cloud. The app runs entirely on Atlassian Forge, so drafts live in Forge storage inside the customer's own Jira site. No external servers, no data egress, no tracking.
- Scope: load the active sprint, the backlog, a project or any JQL query into one table.
- Estimating: story points, original estimate and remaining estimate, edited inline or in bulk. Five scales: Fibonacci, Modified Fibonacci (the default), Powers of 2, Linear and T-Shirt Sizes. Totals update live and can be broken down by epic, assignee, label or type.
- Drafts: work is saved to a private draft first; sharing it makes a team draft the whole team can review. Nothing reaches Jira until someone reviews the Sprint Preview and publishes.
- Free tier: the estimation table, private and team drafts, totals and the Sprint Preview. A free tier can estimate but cannot write to Jira.
- Pro tier: publishing the estimates to Jira (and retrying a failed publish), CSV export, per-assignee workload with capacity warnings, estimation history per issue, and target velocity calculated from closed sprints. Pro is a subscription sold through the Atlassian Marketplace, which handles all billing; current prices and any free allowance are on the listing's pricing tab.
- Install: Atlassian Marketplace, "Scope Planner – Bulk Story Points & Time Estimates for Jira".
- Support: support@dsplugins.dev, answered by the people who build the app.

## Scope Planner

- [Scope Planner – Bulk Story Point & Sprint Estimation for Jira](https://dsplugins.dev/): Estimate story points and time for a whole Jira sprint, backlog or any JQL in one table. Review every change, then publish to Jira in one pass.
- [Scope Planner — User Guide](https://dsplugins.dev/guide/): Scope Planner user guide: setup, the estimation table, drafts, Sprint Preview, publishing, licensing and troubleshooting.

## Articles

- [Articles on Jira estimation and sprint planning](https://dsplugins.dev/articles/): Practical articles on estimating in Jira: story points, bulk editing, story points vs. hours, sprint velocity and velocity per assignee.
- [How to Bulk Edit Story Points in Jira: 4 Ways](https://dsplugins.dev/articles/bulk-edit-story-points-in-jira/): Set story points on many Jira issues at once: bulk change for one shared value, CSV import or a table for different values, with the permissions and limits.
- [Story Points vs Hours in Jira: Which to Use](https://dsplugins.dev/articles/story-points-vs-time-estimates/): Story points or hours in Jira: what Story Points, Original and Remaining Estimate are for, which field the board reads, and whether a point equals hours.
- [How to Calculate Velocity in Jira: Formula & Example](https://dsplugins.dev/articles/sprint-velocity-in-jira/): How to calculate sprint velocity in Jira: the formula, a worked example, what the Velocity Chart counts, sprint completion rate and scope change.
- [Individual Velocity in Jira: Velocity per Assignee](https://dsplugins.dev/articles/velocity-per-assignee-in-jira/): Jira has no individual velocity report. How to get story points per assignee from a search export, the sprint trap to avoid, and why not to judge people by it.
- [Story Points in Jira: What They Are, How to Add Them](https://dsplugins.dev/articles/story-points-in-jira/): Story points in Jira: what they are, how to turn estimation on, add points to work items, fix a missing Story Points field and find them with JQL.
